title: P0.2 Public Identity Onboarding UI

permissions.reason: Signup, activation and password recovery are intentionally public identity flows; Core remains the credential and authorization authority.

database.reason: The UI introduces no FAIR CRM persistence.

migration.reason: No FAIR CRM schema or permission-catalog change is required.

permissions.reason: These routes are public by contract and must not require product RBAC.

backend.reason: The thin FAIR CRM backend bridge was delivered separately in CRM-BE-01/02.

api.reason: This phase consumes the already-delivered FAIR CRM auth bridge without changing its HTTP contract.

tenant_isolation.reason: No product data query or tenant-scoped backend behavior is changed by this UI-only phase.

audit.reason: Identity audit evidence is emitted by Core; the product UI adds no independent audit stream.

ui_permissions.reason: The routes are intentionally public and have no permission-gated controls.

menu.reason: Public auth routes are not application navigation-menu entries.

backend_tests.reason: Backend bridge tests were delivered in CRM-BE-02 and backend code is unchanged here.

runtime_authorization.reason: Public auth is intentionally unauthenticated; Core validates one-time tokens and credentials server-side.

notes: Public pages render outside AuthProvider so no product session is required. Activation/reset action tokens are captured from the link, removed from the address bar after initial render, never displayed/logged, and passed only to the FAIR CRM bridge/Core.
